title: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919
format: 16:9 documentary, English narration, Western YouTube audience
creativeApproach: Archival-first historical documentary. The visual language moves from quiet observational frames to a short, controlled rupture sequence, then slows for rescue, loss, accountability and reflection.
visualRules: Prioritize Boston City Archives, Boston Public Library, and other clearly rights-labeled historical images.
Label maps, diagrams, and any generated reconstruction as explanatory graphics.
Do not use unrelated stock footage as if it depicts the 1919 event.
Keep motion subtle on archival stills; use cuts for evidence and dissolves for reflection.
Use restrained typography, warm archival neutrals, charcoal backgrounds, and amber accents.
No sensational gore, invented eyewitness shots, or unsupported numerical claims.

scenes.title: Cold open: the sound
scenes.narration: In January 1919, one of Boston's strangest disasters began with a sound residents thought might be a train.
scenes.visualQuery: A quiet 1919 North End street; distant elevated train silhouette; sudden metallic shudder interrupts stillness.

scenes.title: The tank above the neighborhood
scenes.narration: On Commercial Street, in the city's North End, a steel tank stood beside homes, workplaces, and an elevated railway. It was roughly five stories tall, and it held millions of gallons of industrial molasses.

scenes.title: A warning hiding in plain sight
scenes.narration: The tank belonged to Purity Distilling Company. Built only a few years earlier, it had already become part of everyday neighborhood life. Residents had seen it leak. Some remembered the metal groaning when it was full. Those warning signs did not stop the tank from being used.

scenes.title: A wave through Commercial Street
scenes.narration: Around 2.3 million gallons of molasses burst into the streets. The dark wave tore through the waterfront district, smashing buildings, sweeping away vehicles, and damaging the elevated railway. A nearby firehouse was badly hit.

scenes.title: Not a harmless flood
scenes.narration: This was not a harmless flood of syrup. The moving mass trapped people and animals. As it spread, debris became entangled in the thick liquid, making escape and rescue extraordinarily difficult.

scenes.narration: The final toll was devastating: twenty-one people died, and around one hundred and fifty were injured.

scenes.title: The cleanup
scenes.narration: In the days that followed, crews faced another problem. The molasses hardened in the winter air. Workers pumped seawater through the streets and hauled away debris, but cleanup took weeks.

scenes.title: The lesson
scenes.narration: The Great Molasses Flood is remembered for its bizarre image: a city street overwhelmed by something sweet. But its real lesson is not about molasses. It is about ignored warnings, weak engineering, and the human cost when industrial safety is treated as an afterthought.
